name: Earth Planetary Sciences (BS)

rules.name: Narrative Text
rules.desc:
Earth and Planetary Sciences is an interdisciplinary field that draws heavily on the other sciences. Students are encouraged to supplement their major coursework with classes in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, and Biology, based on their background, goals, and interests, in consultation with their faculty advisor.
Major Requirements (60 units):

• Core: 21 units

• Breadth in Discipline: 27 units

• Depth in Discipline: 6 units

• WIM: 3 units

• Capstone: 3 units

rules.name: Earth and Planetary Sciences Foundation (21 units)
rules.desc: Students must complete 6 courses that introduce the properties of planetary materials, the processes that change the Earth and other planets, and the timescales over which those processes act. These courses provide a broad foundational knowledge that can lead to specialization in many different geological and environmental sciences disciplines.

rules.name: Electives (27 units)
rules.desc:
Students select from a range of 100-level elective geoscience courses, providing exposure to diverse fields. These courses include classroom lectures, often supplemented with field and laboratory components.
Students are required to complete 27 units, of which 18 must be from EPS.

rules.name: Research (6 units)
rules.desc:
Students are required to complete 6 units of hands-on scientific research under the guidance of one or more faculty mentors. All majors must engage in hands-on research using the scientific method under faculty mentorship. Each student is required to complete 6 units of research under the guidance of one or more faculty mentors. The culmination of this research is a thesis that is potentially suitable for submission to a disciplinary journal.
Example: Students can enroll in 4 units of EPS 192 and 2 units of EPS 197 to equal the minimum 6 units required for Depth in Discipline.
rules.notes: Senior Thesis (for seniors who wish to take writing units on a thesis based on research in 192 or as a summer research fellow).

rules.name: WIM (3 units)
rules.desc: Writing in the Major courses provides students with opportunities to develop writing skills in the context of their major fields. It begins the process of learning to write effectively in discipline-specific formats and styles.

rules.name: EPS Capstone Options (3 units)
rules.desc:
Students may fulfill the capstone requirement through either a departmental field study program or an independent capstone research project. The field study option includes a minimum of six weeks of field research with training in field techniques, including mapping, and a written report. The research project option requires students to present their findings through written reports and oral presentations.
Contact the EPS Student Services Team in the department for enrollment guidance.

children.name: Option 1 - Research in the Field
children.desc:
The first option is participation in a departmental field study program, which includes a minimum of six weeks of field research. These month-long courses provide students with the opportunity to collect data in the field as part of a team-based investigation of research questions, under the guidance of faculty and graduate students. Students learn and apply field techniques, including mapping, and complete a written report documenting their work. Topics and locations vary.
Rule Note: Juniors planning to enroll in this summer field course should contact the EPS Student Services Team during the Winter or Spring Quarter, prior to the summer offering, for information regarding the course location, tuition, enrollment procedures, and other logistical details.
children.notes: Students may enroll for a minimum of 1 unit per quarter and may repeat enrollment for credit, up to a maximum of 3 units

children.name: Option 2 - Scientific Knowledge Applied to Real-World Challenges
children.desc:
Alternatively, students may fulfill the requirement by completing an independent capstone research project. In this option, students apply their geoscience background to design and address real-world problems. They are expected to present their findings through written reports and oral presentations.
Evaluation may include participation in SDSS departmental symposia or assessment by non-profit specialists, and must take place within the year of enrollment in the capstone course. All self-designed capstone projects must be submitted to and approved by the Director of Undergraduate Studies prior to enrollment.
children.notes: Students may enroll for a minimum of 1 unit per quarter and may repeat enrollment for credit, up to a maximum of 3 units

rules.name: Overview & Requirements
rules.desc:
The honors program provides an opportunity for year-long independent study and research on a topic of particular interest, culminating in a written thesis. Students select research topics in consultation with the faculty advisor of their choice. Research undertaken for the honors program may be theoretical, field, experimental, or a combination of these approaches. The honors program is open to students with a GPA of at least 3.0 in all university coursework. Modest financial support is available from several sources to help defray laboratory and field expenses incurred in conjunction with honors research.
To apply, please visit: https://epsci.stanford.edu/academics-admissions/undergraduate-program/honors-program
To receive a Bachelor of Science with honors designation, students are required to:

• Submit a formal written report to both the student’s research advisor and the second faculty member no later than the fourth week of the student’s final quarter, or by a date preferred by the research advisor.

• Obtain advisor (first reader) approval on the report and a second faculty member (second reader). Submit the Bachelor of Science with Honors Completion Verification Signature Form to the department before graduation, ideally by the University’s thesis submission deadline for the quarter.

• Students may choose to submit their paper to the Stanford Digital Repository—please contact the EPS Student Services Team for more information.

• Students must present their research at a public seminar approved by the DUS. The EPS department typically hosts an Undergraduate Symposium or coordinates with the student EPS Brown Bag seminars at the end of May each year, providing an opportunity for BSH students to present their research.
The decision whether a given research project merits an award of honors will be made jointly by the student’s faculty advisor, second reader, and the Undergraduate Program Director, and will be based on the quality of both the honors work and the student’s other work in earth sciences.
rules.notes:
Enroll in EPS 199 under your research faculty advisor. 9 units total are required by year-end, which can be distributed throughout senior year as needed.
Optional: Honors students in EPS are also eligible for University awards such as the Firestone Medal, which is awarded by Academic Advising for exceptional theses. Students who wish to be considered for University awards must submit the Bachelor of Science with Honors Completion Verification Signature Form by the end of the Winter Quarter of their graduating year.

rules.name: Honors report approved by two readers and presented

gpa: Stanford undergraduates must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.0 to remain in good academic standing and graduate. While the university calculates GPA using a traditional 4.0 scale, competitive admissions averages hover near a 3.94, and individual class rankings are not calculated.
grading:
Students must earn letter grades in all core, breadth, WIM, and capstone courses.
General University Grading System: https://studentservices.stanford.edu/my-academics/evaluations-exams-grades/grades/general-university-grading-system
Students are responsible for checking their final grades at the end of each quarter. If incomplete grades (I), Grade Not Reported (GNR), or No Credit (NC) appear on the end-of-quarter grade report, students should immediately check with their instructor. The Assistant Director of Student Services can assist students and instructors in clearing missing and incomplete grades by forwarding the appropriate instructions and/or university forms.
transferPolicy:
Undergraduate Transfer Credit: Stanford University may grant transfer credit for work completed at regionally accredited institutions or internationally recognized colleges and universities. No more than 45 (90 for transfer students) quarter units of credit for external work may be counted toward a Stanford bachelor's degree.
Up to 10 units of transfer credit may be counted toward major requirements, subject to approval by the Director of Undergraduate Studies and provided the coursework is deemed relevant to the department's program.
reviewNotes: The core, breadth, WIM and capstone courses must be letter graded; research units need not be. You take the six foundation courses, 27 units of electives with at most 9 outside EPS, 6 units of research in EPS 192 or 197, EPS 150 for Writing in the Major, and 3 units of EPS 190 or EPS 193 for the capstone (repeat enrollments count), for 60 units. Your advisor checks the 2.0 GPA, approval of a self-designed capstone, and transfer credit (at most 10 units). Honors adds 9 units of EPS 199, a 3.0 GPA, and a report approved by two readers and presented. Left: the Bulletin calls the foundation 21 units, but its six courses carry 20 in the catalog, so the minimum in every rule comes to 59 and the audit asks for one more unit toward the 60.
